match_note: Round 1 reviewed manuscript NCOMMS-25-63869-T carries the exact v1 title. Every referee pointer resolves in v1: Fig. S3 with no-RF and -18 dBm traces and the SC2 close-up S3c, Fig. S5b integrated voltage, Fig. 3c at 67.5 MHz, the 40 x 67 x 18 junction estimate and N_j = 430, 'quasi-four-probe configuration' in the SI, and the quoted sentences (quantum simulator, gauge-gravity duality, level spacing, 'We reiterate that the reentrance appears only upon the application of RF current'). v1 shows a single device and no I-V curves, as the referees say. R1's round 1 report is empty in the main body and appears as an attachment at the end of the file (also quoted in the rebuttal). Round 2: R1 and R2 sign off; R3 has no round 2 report.

concerns.quote: the results were measured on only one device. As reproducibility is a key concept for science ... I ask for measurements on different devices.
concerns.summary: All data come from a single device; the referees ask whether the effect is easily observed and request measurements on further devices, also to probe device variability of the energy scales and giant Shapiro steps.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: there can be spikes in dV/dI at the edges of regions showing Shapiro steps, including in the RCSJ simulations ... Can the authors distinguish their insulating regime from the dV/dI 'spikes'
concerns.summary: The high-resistance 'insulating' region might be an ordinary RCSJ Shapiro-step dV/dI spike rather than a phase-slip insulator.

concerns.quote: Does the RF drive ever make the sample appear 'more superconducting' compared to no RF drive? ... in particular near Tc
concerns.summary: Asks whether RF drive enhances superconductivity near Tc, which would hint at RF-promoted phase synchronization.

concerns.quote: In Fig. S3 the no RF and -18 dBm colors are almost imperceptibly different ... I request the authors change the colors/plot layout to make the no RF data completely clear.
concerns.summary: Fig. S3 colors make the no-RF trace indistinguishable from -18 dBm, so absence of reentrance without RF cannot be read off.

concerns.quote: can you show resistance versus temperature measurements (raw data) with identical inputs but with and without RF-signal ?
concerns.summary: Both referees ask for a clear with-versus-without-RF R(T) comparison to establish that reentrance really requires RF drive.

concerns.quote: the authors never show current-voltage characteristics (IVCs) of their samples ... it would be very helpful to see representative IVCs
concerns.summary: No I-V curves are shown; R2 wants IVCs in SC1, insulating, SC2 and normal regions, R3 wants the usual I-V curves demonstrating Shapiro steps.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: I had a lot of difficulties to understand what superconducting re-entrance behavior(s) the authors is(are) referring to ... raw data are needed both for clarity and to check for experimental rigor.
concerns.summary: The color-plot presentation makes it unclear which reentrance is claimed; raw line-cut data are needed for clarity and to judge rigor.

concerns.quote: From the color plot the re-entrance behavior is not obvious as there is no dissipationless superconducting state (dark blue), neither « Shapiro steps »
concerns.summary: Fig. 1a does not visibly show reentrance with RF power, a dissipationless state, or labeled Shapiro steps; the meaning of 'tuned by RF power' needs clarifying.

concerns.quote: the RF-tuning on the SC1-phase is pretty classic: an increased RF-power, results in an increased RF-current, results in a decreased critical current/gap/EJ
concerns.summary: Suppression of SC1 by RF power has an ordinary explanation (total current I_b + I_RF exceeds the critical current) that the text should state.

concerns.quote: From the raw data presented in the supplementary figS3 the dissipationless superconducting state reentrant is not demonstrated: the resistance is far from being null
concerns.summary: The reentrant SC2 state in Fig. S3 does not show zero resistance, so true reentrant superconductivity is not demonstrated.

concerns.quote: (and the data are incomplete, points are missing)
concerns.summary: Fig. S3 R(T) traces have missing data points.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Probable reentrant superconductivity with temperature (with nonzero resistance) has already been reported in (highly) resistive granular aluminum ... Can you (re)explain the novelty
concerns.summary: Reentrance in granular aluminum without RF was reported by Jaeger et al. 1989, Wu and Adams 1994 and Levy-Bertrand et al. 2019; cite them and explain novelty.

concerns.quote: A RF power P_RF=-20dBm is probably like not RF-signal and yet you observed (a non zero) re-entrance superconductivity
concerns.summary: Reentrance at negligible RF power suggests it is intrinsic to the film rather than RF-induced, contradicting the claim that it appears only with RF.

concerns.quote: The re-entrance seems wider in temperature (thus more robust) at low RF-power. Any comments ?
concerns.summary: Asks why the reentrant region is widest at the lowest RF power.

concerns.quote: I do not see the Shapiro steps in fig 3. Is fig3c a simulation ?
concerns.summary: Shapiro steps are not visible in Fig. 3 and it is unclear whether Fig. 3c is data or simulation.

concerns.quote: I do not understand how the authors estimate the number of inter-grain JJs [for me Nx=120nm/(2x5nm+1nm)=24 ...] Can the authors (re)explain the estimation procedure?
concerns.summary: The geometric junction-count estimate (40 x 67 x 18) does not match the referee's own calculation and needs explaining.

concerns.quote: The actual measurement set-up needs to be clarified. In particular the expression «quasi-four-probe configuration» ... Can you provide an accurate scheme of the actual geometry ?
concerns.summary: The quasi-four-probe geometry is unclear and needs a schematic and explanation in the main text.

concerns.quote: Do you filter out the ac-voltage (coming from the RF-current) from the dc-voltage?
concerns.summary: Asks whether the RF voltage is filtered from the DC voltage measurement, i.e. whether RF pickup could contaminate the signal.

concerns.quote: Do you mesure the resulting RF-current ?
concerns.summary: The RF current actually delivered to the device is not measured.

concerns.quote: I completely disagree with the last sentence ... The behavior of granular aluminum is far from that of a single-junction ... neither how a single experimental device could be used for quantum simulations.
concerns.summary: The claim that the system reaches a single-junction regime and serves as a quantum simulator is overstated.

concerns.quote: I suggest you remove the following sentence that is cryptic to me: «Reentrant superconductivity has also been explored through gauge-gravity duality
concerns.summary: The gauge-gravity duality sentence is cryptic and should be removed.

concerns.quote: I suggest you elaborate more on the following sentence or you remove it: «Additionally, the electronic level spacing within each island exceeds both Ec and the superconducting gap
concerns.summary: The level-spacing statement and its claimed insensitivity to microscopic details needs justification.

first_round.quote: Overall I find the study to be of high quality and that it is suitable for publication, subject to addressing some concerns below.

The paper is generally suitable for Nature Communications... These plots could be presented in the Supplementary Information section. With these or a comparable modification I will be happy to recommend the manuscript for publication
I therefore ask the authors to make significant changes to the manuscript so that the experimental rigor of their work becomes clear... I ask for measurements on different devices.

recommendations.note: No transfer from another journal is indicated; Version 0 is the first round in this file. Reviewer #1's Version 0 remarks are blank in the main report section. Their first-round report appears as an attachment at the end of the file (page 13), and it is the basis for R1's recommendation. R1 asks questions, including whether the effect was seen in multiple devices, rather than demanding new data, so it is inferred as minor revision. R2 asks only for current-voltage curves to go in the Supplementary Information, so it is inferred as minor revision. R3 demands significant changes and measurements on additional devices, so it is inferred as major revision. No referee co-signed another's report.
recommendations.label: contested
